body:
10,000 Trees in Waterloo
The City of Waterloo is planting 10,000 new trees across parks and public spaces. This project page will provide residents with information on where new trees will be planted and how the city is enhancing its urban forest.
The trees will be planted over between 2025 to 2026, with 2027 dedicated to maintaining the planted trees.
Follow this project by clicking
+Follow
in the banner to:
See the planned tree planting locations.
Learn about the types of trees being planted.
Track the progress of plantings as they happen.
Why we're planting
We're planting to keep our tree canopy healthy, to grow a more diverse mix of trees and to reduce the amount of grass that needs be mowed.
Learn more
How we help newly planted trees thrive
Our planting methods follow current research and best practices, which have helped us achieve high survival rates, including a 95% success rate during summer planting as part of this project.
Learn more
Tree planting locations
Explore this map to see where trees are planned in Waterloo.
Note: Locations are subject to change. Each planned tree is represented by a yellow dot. Once a tree has been planted, it will no longer show as a dot on the map. The map will be updated in real time as planting progresses.
